subject: Design and technology

source.title: National curriculum in England: design and technology programmes of study

coverage.yearStructure: key-stage programme; no statutory year-by-year sequence
coverage.ks4: not applicable as a national curriculum programme; design and technology is a KS4 entitlement area

statementPolicy: Controlled paraphrases only. Example content in square brackets and other non-statutory material are not represented as statutory objectives.

KS1.summary: Design purposeful, functional and appealing products for users using design criteria.
Generate, develop, model and communicate ideas through discussion, drawing, templates, mock-ups and appropriate digital tools.
Select and use a range of tools and equipment for practical tasks.
Select materials and components, including construction materials, textiles and ingredients, according to their characteristics.
Evaluate ideas and products against design criteria.
Build structures and explore ways to make them stronger, stiffer and more stable.
Explore and use mechanisms such as levers, sliders, wheels and axles in products.
Use basic principles of a healthy and varied diet when preparing dishes.

KS2.summary: Use research and design criteria to develop innovative, functional and appealing products for particular users.
Generate, develop, model and communicate ideas using discussion, annotated sketches, diagrams, prototypes, pattern pieces and computer-aided design.
Select and use a wider range of tools and equipment accurately for practical tasks.
Select materials and components according to functional properties and aesthetic qualities.
Evaluate ideas and products against design criteria, consider others' views and improve work.
Understand how key events and individuals in design and technology have helped shape the world.
Apply understanding of how to strengthen, stiffen and reinforce more complex structures.
Understand and use mechanical systems such as gears, pulleys, cams, levers and linkages in products.
Understand and use electrical systems in products.
Apply computing to program, monitor and control products.
Understand and apply principles of a healthy and varied diet.
Prepare and cook a variety of predominantly savoury dishes using a range of cooking techniques.
Understand seasonality and where and how ingredients are grown, reared, caught and processed.

KS3.summary: Use research and exploration to identify and understand user needs, including through consideration of different cultures.
Identify and solve design problems and reformulate problems when required.
Develop specifications for innovative, functional and appealing products that respond to needs in varied situations.
Use varied approaches to generate creative ideas and avoid stereotypical responses.
Develop and communicate ideas through annotated sketches, detailed plans, 3-D and mathematical modelling, oral and digital presentations.
Select and use specialist tools, techniques, processes, equipment and machinery precisely, including computer-aided manufacture.
Select a wider and more complex range of materials, components and ingredients according to their properties.
Analyse the work of past and present professionals to broaden understanding of design and technology.
Test, evaluate and refine ideas and products against a specification using views of intended users and other interested groups.
Understand developments in design and technology, their impact on people, society and the environment, and the responsibilities of designers, engineers and technologists.
Understand and use material properties and structural performance to achieve functioning solutions.
Understand how advanced mechanical systems enable changes in movement and force.
Understand how advanced electrical and electronic systems can be powered and used in products.
Apply computing and electronics to embed intelligence in products that respond to inputs and control outputs using programmable components.
Understand and apply principles of nutrition and health.
Cook a repertoire of predominantly savoury dishes that supports a healthy and varied diet.
Become competent in a range of cooking techniques and adapt recipes using knowledge of taste, texture and smell.
Understand the source, seasonality and characteristics of a broad range of ingredients.
